## Subjective

74yo M, established patient with HFrEF (EF 30%) post-MI 2022, presents w/ 5-day h/o progressive lower extremity edema, dyspnea on exertion now after walking ~10 ft (was prior 1/2 block) (location: bilateral legs, chest; quality: tightness on exertion; severity: limiting ADLs; duration: 5 days progressive; timing: worse at night, requiring 3 pillows now vs prior 1; associated symptoms: 6 lb weight gain over 5 days, dry cough at night). Denies chest pain at rest, syncope, palpitations. Compliant with all meds per pill counts brought to visit: metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, spironolactone, furosemide 40mg daily, atorvastatin, ASA 81. Diet: admits to take-out meals over weekend (high sodium). FHx: noncontributory beyond CAD. SHx: lives alone, retired, no tobacco/EtOH.

## Objective

VS: BP 138/82, HR 92 (regular), RR 22, T 98.2°F, SpO2 92% on RA (baseline 96%), weight 188 lb (up 6 lb from 2 weeks prior). Gen: mild distress, can speak in full sentences. HEENT: JVD ~10 cm. Cardiac: RRR, faint S3 audible, no murmurs. Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid-lung fields, no wheezing. Abdomen: soft, NT, no HSM. Extremities: 2+ pitting edema bilateral up to knees, distal pulses 2+, warm. Neuro: A&O×3, no focal deficits.

CXR (in office): cardiomegaly stable, mild bilateral pulmonary congestion, no infiltrate. BNP 1820 (baseline ~600). BMP: Cr 1.4 (baseline 1.2), K 4.0, Na 138.

## Assessment

1. Acute on chronic systolic CHF exacerbation, NYHA class III today (I50.23) — likely dietary indiscretion + possible early diuretic resistance
2. Stage IIIa CKD (N18.31), worsening with diuresis caution
3. CAD s/p MI 2022 (I25.10)
4. HTN (I10) — at goal currently

## Plan

Outpatient diuresis trial vs. admission discussed at length with patient — patient strongly prefers outpatient given alertness, ability to walk to bathroom, family check-in plans, and historical successful outpatient management.

Decision: outpatient management with strict return precautions.

- Furosemide increased to 80mg PO daily ×3 days, then re-evaluate; metolazone 2.5mg added qAM × 3 days only (boost); spironolactone continued; recheck BMP in 48 hours (lab order placed).
- Sodium restriction emphasized (<2g/day), fluid restriction <2L/day.
- Weight log daily, call if up 2 lb in 24 hr or 4 lb in 3 days.
- Patient given list: dyspnea at rest, orthopnea worsening, syncope, chest pain, fingerstick >180 (he's borderline pre-DM), or weight up 4+ lb → call/return/911.
- Cardiology notified, available for phone consultation as needed.
- F/u 48 hr for symptom + weight check + BMP review. If no improvement → admit.

Reviewed cardiology echo from 6 months ago (EF 30%) and last admit discharge summary (Sept 2025, similar exacerbation, responded to IV diuresis × 36 hr). Independent interpretation of today's CXR + BNP integrated with clinical picture.

Discussed and documented joint decision to defer admission given patient stability, supports, reliable f/u. Captured as decision-re-hospitalization for MDM purposes.
